reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, resource-level rubric, fresh-review framework, PaymentNotice context, full StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, local R4/R6 PaymentNotice StructureDefinitions, and the provider/reporter SearchParameters used as supporting evidence. Direct behavior reports had no PaymentNotice-specific findings; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior was considered only as context.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 PaymentNotice was FMM 2/trial-use, so it does not carry the strong compatibility burden of normative or FMM 5 content. The financial-management domain still makes attribution, reconciliation, and audit effects relevant when a local break changes payment-party meaning.

overall.oneLineConclusion: PaymentNotice keeps its resource identity and is mostly stable; the provider-to-reporter rename is the main avoidable forward break, so compatibility preservation still has high per-change value.

reasoning.thesisMd: PaymentNotice is not removed, split, or deeply remodeled in R6. The local content model remains recognizable, with one hard R4-to-R6 instance/API break (`provider` removed in favor of `reporter`), one important reverse-direction/nullability change (`payment` no longer required), one optional additive field (`statusReason`), and one non-required terminology-strength increase (`paymentStatus`). That supports targeted migration work, not a resource-level conclusion that a major migration program already dominates.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: Forward R4-to-R6 migration is concentrated on `PaymentNotice.provider`: R4 instances containing that element fail strict R6 validation unless transformed, and implementers must decide whether the R4 provider responsible for services is truly the R6 party reporting the notice. R6 clients must also handle `payment` as optional, and R6-to-R4 downgrade paths need policy for omitted `payment` and populated `statusReason`. The remaining local elements, reference targets, required fields, modifier status behavior, and resource identity are stable enough that most migration is targeted rather than model-wide.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the resource is mostly stable, preventing individual avoidable breaks remains valuable. A migration program is not already unavoidable at the whole-resource level, so low-cost compatibility measures such as retaining a deprecated `provider` element, documenting a safe mapping boundary, or preserving a provider search alias could materially reduce validation, generated-code, search-client, and audit risk. FMM 2 lowers the standards burden but does not make financial attribution breaks unimportant.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest less-breaking opportunity is the `provider`/`reporter` change: R6 could have kept `provider` as a deprecated legacy element or search alias while adding `reporter`, or retained the old wire name if the intended role was not actually distinct. That would create some duplicate-field or naming tension, but it is a plausible, modest-cost compatibility design worth standards review. By contrast, making `payment` optional appears to serve legitimate R6 lifecycle flexibility; preserving R4's required cardinality or adding conditional rules would reduce downgrade risk but also constrain that goal. `statusReason` is additive, and the `paymentStatus` binding remains non-required, so neither materially changes the resource-level leverage conclusion.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinitions, SearchParameters, or HTTP REST behavior findings were assigned to PaymentNotice in the supplied context. The supporting package evidence does show a PaymentNotice search rename from R4 `provider` (`PaymentNotice.provider`) to R6 `reporter` (`PaymentNotice.reporter`), which amplifies the local element rename for search clients even though it was not reported as a direct behavior finding here. Shared Resource/DomainResource operation and special-search-parameter changes may affect PaymentNotice endpoints in implementations, but they are base-surface context and are not counted as PaymentNotice-specific migration pressure.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = No`, `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, and `preserve-compatibility-per-change`. I agree, but for substantive reasons rather than counts: the hard break is localized to a rename with semantic drift, while the other findings are reverse-direction, additive, or warning-level. The aggregate's warning that the Revisit finding should not be dismissed is also correct.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for local StructureDefinition shape and SearchParameter evidence. Remaining uncertainty comes from the absence of an official R4-to-R6 PaymentNotice change rationale, the R6 ballot-build status, and incomplete local terminology expansion evidence for `payment-status`.

findingConsiderations.title: PaymentNotice.provider was replaced by PaymentNotice.reporter
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the only local hard R4-to-R6 instance break and the clearest standards-review issue. It changes the wire element and matching search surface, and the definitions are not a guaranteed semantic synonym: a provider responsible for services can differ from the party reporting the payment notice.

findingConsiderations.title: PaymentNotice.payment is no longer required in R6
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This does not invalidate valid R4 instances moving forward, so it does not make a major R4-to-R6 migration unavoidable. It is still operationally important because R6 instances may lack the PaymentReconciliation link that R4 workflows treated as mandatory, creating nullability and downgrade policy work.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional PaymentNotice.statusReason
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The element is optional and additive for R4-to-R6 migration. It may need extension or omission policy when downgrading to R4, but it does not support a resource-level migration-program conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: PaymentNotice.paymentStatus binding strengthened from example to preferred
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The binding remains non-required, so old CodeableConcept values are not made invalid in the base resource. This may create warning-level or profiling pressure, but it is not a hard compatibility break.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource operation change can affect implementations that expose base operations on PaymentNotice instances, but it is not PaymentNotice-specific and should be scored in the Resource/base behavior review rather than used to inflate this resource's local migration burden.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is shared Resource/DomainResource search context. It may matter to generic clients, but it does not change the PaymentNotice-specific conclusion because no direct PaymentNotice behavior finding was supplied.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit the `provider` to `reporter` transition before finalizing R6: either preserve a deprecated/alias `provider` path or explicitly justify why the semantic correction outweighs the validation, search, generated-code, and financial-attribution break.

Publish migration guidance for PaymentNotice distinguishing mechanical rename cases from cases where `provider` and `reporter` are different business actors, and define policy for R6 notices that omit `payment` when downgrading or integrating with R4-era reconciliation workflows.
Confirm the final R6 `payment-status` terminology expansion and document that the strengthened binding remains preferred guidance, not a base invalidation of existing local codes.

caveats: No official R4-to-R6 PaymentNotice diff or change rationale was available in the supplied local inputs.
The reviewed R6 package is 6.0.0-ballot4, so conclusions should be rechecked against final published R6 content.
Local terminology evidence lacked complete payment-status expansion and R6 local CodeSystem evidence.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only and not scored as PaymentNotice-specific findings.
